question: How is the range of motion (the fan: where the next step's node may be set) drawn, so that one style reads across every unit type? Alex: 'I want to look at the design of the acceptable range of motion indicator for planes. Is there a style that makes more sense across all unit types? Should we just have a little shaded area where you can set the node? Show me some options before commiting this.'
source: scripts/ui/boards/motion_range_board_shot.gd: the running sandbox (scripts/app/sandbox.gd) over the real map, scenario variants/motion-range/scenario.json (seed 20261009, water on, fog off), the game's own planner (scripts/ui/motion_planner.gd _draw_fan), photographed once per option with ONLY data/ui/ui.json planner.fan.mode changed

held_constant.units: a light fighter and the bomber over open ground, a tank on the village road, its next step starting 33 m from the bridge's middle (it stands 53 m from it, one step planned), the cruiser beside the east coast (3594, 1300) heading west; all of one side (side_a, brick red), each flown two real turns so its ribbon is the game's, one or two steps planned, the unit selected; the next step's fan is up with the plan line, ghosts and speed labels
held_constant.crop_apex: the fan's apex (the last planned step, or the unit) falls at the same pixel in every crop of a zoom: (320, 85), (150, 55), (130, 40); the crops of 0.35 and 0.2 put it nearer the left so the planes and the start of their ribbon are in
held_constant.cone_wash: OFF in the grid (planner.cones.shown is another session's; the weapon-arcs button), shown once for the light fighter
held_constant.fog: off in this rig (scenario view.fog false), so every crop shows the drawn map
held_constant.ship_rig: the cruiser's crops are drawn with the planner raised above the marker layer, because today the hull covers the fan (shown separately); a rig action, not a game change
held_constant.decisions_in_force: shadow strength 0.44; pen 'shadow_side'; side colours brick red (allies) and slate blue (axis); the ribbon trail (wingtip-trails D, all moving units); cones as a colour wash for the selected unit; planes at their own scale

parameter: data/ui/ui.json#planner.fan.mode (ribs | shade | wash_rim | stipple | hatch | rim_ticks) and planner.fan.<mode> for each one's numbers and colour roles (roles fan_shade, fan_wash, fan_rim, fan_dot, fan_hatch, fan_rim_quiet, fan_centre, fan_tick in ui.json roles)

options.name: A
options.title: Today: outline, a faint wash and ribs
options.description: The game as it is: an inked outline (78%, 1.2 px), a faint wash inside it (10%), a rib across the band for each sampled turn and two dashed spokes back to the apex.

options.name: B
options.title: A shaded area, no outline (Alex's idea)
options.description: Just the region, flat ink at 30%: no outline, no ribs, no spokes. The node is set 'in the shade'. Alex's own idea. The tone is raised from today's wash (10%) because with no outline the tone alone has to show the edge.

options.name: C
options.title: Wash and a thin inked rim
options.description: A wash (14%) under one thin rim (0.9 px at 50%): the shaded area with its edge said once, in the line's own weight. No ribs, no spokes.

options.name: D
options.title: Stipple
options.description: Ink dots (70%, 1.8 px) on a jittered grid (3.6 px cells) inside the region, no outline at all: the map's own grain and the cone board's stipple. The edge is where the dots stop.

options.name: E
options.title: Hatch
options.description: 45 degree ink strokes (55%, 0.8 px) 4.0 px apart, cut to the region, no outline: the map's hachures. On a band this thin it reads as a ladder.

options.name: F
options.title: Quiet rim, and ticks for the slowest and the fastest reach
options.description: A quiet rim (0.9 px at 45%) and a faint ruler from the apex along the centre (22%), with a bar across it at the slowest reach (the near edge) and at the fastest (the far edge): as the cone board's outline look carries range ticks. No fill.

palette_check.hue: No option adds a hue: every fan mark is INK (L 0.325) at an alpha, over PAPER (L 0.847). The roles, with the lightness each gives over the paper, are in `roles`. The unit's side accent appears only in the cone wash under the fan (side_a at 7 to 30%) and in the ribbon, never in the fan.
palette_check.lightness: A ramp off the paper: wash 14%, today's wash 10%, centre line 22%, shade 30%, rim 45 to 50%, hatch 55%, dots 70%, ticks 80% (today's rim is 78% and its ribs 20%).
palette_check.material: linework: a rim, ticks, hatch strokes, dots; or a wash. No new colour, no hex in draw code (roles in data).

recommendation_proposed: C, a wash under one thin rim, no ribs and no spokes, for every unit type (PROPOSED by builder BM; Alex decides). The region is a thin arc for the planes, a small wedge for the tank and a speck for the cruiser, and the ribs and spokes are most of today's ink, so Alex's instinct is right that they are not what tells a player where a node can go. But a tone alone (B) is the first thing to vanish where the region is smallest and the ground busiest (the fighter's is a 3 by 24 px streak at the start zoom, over trees), so one thin rim keeps it findable: C is the same two marks on every unit at every zoom, in ink only. D and E break up on a 9 px band (a dotted line, a ladder). F is the quietest and the only look that says the slowest and the fastest reach, so it is the one to keep in mind if Alex wants the extent shown. None of them fixes the cruiser: its region is under its own hull today.
how_to_switch: set planner.fan.mode in data/ui/ui.json to the option's mode; nothing else changes
